html:
The largest cliff dwelling in North America, built by the Ancestral Puebloans in an alcove of a canyon wall at Mesa Verde in southwestern Colorado. Tree-ring dates show most of it was built between about 1190 and 1260.

It holds about 150 rooms and more than 20 kivas, the round sunken rooms used for ceremony and meeting. The walls are of shaped sandstone set in mortar and once plastered and painted. Perhaps 100 people lived there, and it may also have been a centre for gatherings of the wider community. Farmers grew maize, beans and squash on the mesa top above.

People moved into the cliffs after centuries of living on the mesa, perhaps for defence or shelter. By about 1300 the whole region was abandoned, during a long drought and times of conflict. The people moved south to join the Pueblo communities of New Mexico and Arizona, whose descendants still live there. This was the same people who had earlier built Chaco Canyon.
